force.title: The Real-Estate Reckoning
force.signature: Hybrid work broke the office and higher rates broke the math — capital rotates from offices to logistics, data centers, and housing, and a debt wall forces the reckoning.

A \u00b7 The office breaks: Hybrid work and vacancies gut office values; a maturity wall forces losses.
Dead offices and malls get converted — a remodeling and construction opportunity.
B \u00b7 Where capital rotates: High rates freeze buying and pressure multifamily even as housing stays scarce.
Capital flows to warehouses and data centers — the assets with demand.
Land and ground-lease models become the quiet, durable real-estate bet.
C \u00b7 Hospitality & retail property: Lodging bifurcates and gets financialized as an asset class.
Store closures dump retail real estate onto the market for reuse.
D \u00b7 The tensions: A wave of maturing CRE loans refinancing at higher rates is the sector's tail risk.
Tariffs, labor, and rates raise the cost to build anything new.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: work and rates broke the old real-estate math; logistics, data, and housing win, offices lose.
